details: picklescan before 0.0.22 only considers standard pickle file extensions in the scope for its vulnerability scan. An attacker could craft a malicious model that uses Pickle and include a malicious pickle file with a non-standard file extension. Because the malicious pickle file inclusion is not considered as part of the scope of picklescan, the file would pass security checks and appear to be safe, when it could instead prove to be problematic.

A vulnerability in the GraphCypherQAChain class of langchain-ai/langchain-community version 0.2.5 allows for SQL injection through prompt injection. This vulnerability can lead to unauthorized data manipulation, data exfiltration, denial of service (DoS) by deleting all data, breaches in multi-tenant security environments, and data integrity issues. Attackers can create, update, or delete nodes and relationships without proper authorization, extract sensitive data, disrupt services, access data across different tenants, and compromise the integrity of the database.

cwe.name: Buffer Copy without Checking Size of Input

notes.text: A flaw was found in LibreOffice. When a user imports a specially crafted PDF document with LibreOffice Draw, a heap-based buffer overflow can occur due to improper validation of the stream length. This issue can cause memory corruption, resulting in an application crash.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: libreoffice: heap buffer overflow in PDF import stream handling
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
To exploit this issue, an attacker needs to convince a user to import a specially crafted PDF document. This flaw can cause memory corruption, resulting in an application crash. However, the possibility of arbitrary code execution is not discarded. For these reasons, this vulnerability has been rated with a moderate severity.

Default Red Hat Enterprise Linux security features, including SELinux enforcement, Address Space Layout Randomization (ASLR) and NX (No-Execute) stack protection, significantly increase the difficulty of achieving arbitrary code execution, limiting the impact of this vulnerability.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: The CVSS score(s) listed for this vulnerability do not reflect the associated product's status, and are included for informational purposes to better understand the severity of this vulnerability.
notes.title: CVSS score applicability

remediations.details:
For details on how to apply this update, which includes the changes described in this advisory, refer to:

https://access.redhat.com/articles/11258
Do not import PDF documents from unknown or untrusted sources with LibreOffice Draw.

cwe.name: Inclusion of Functionality from Untrusted Control Sphere

notes.text: A flaw was found in LibreOffice. When linking spreadsheet cell ranges to external data sources in Calc, a document can specify an external Java database driver. By convincing a user to open a specially crafted document, a remote attacker can force the application to download and execute untrusted Java code from a remote location, resulting in arbitrary code execution.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: libreoffice: libreoffice: Arbitrary code execution via remote Java database driver
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Vulnerability in LibreOffice Calc allows execution of untrusted Java code via remote Java database driver paths in spreadsheet cell range links. When an attacker tricks a user into opening a specially crafted spreadsheet document, Calc downloads and executes arbitrary remote Java code under the security context of the logged-in user.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: The CVSS score(s) listed for this vulnerability do not reflect the associated product's status, and are included for informational purposes to better understand the severity of this vulnerability.
notes.title: CVSS score applicability

remediations.details:
For details on how to apply this update, which includes the changes described in this advisory, refer to:

https://access.redhat.com/articles/11258

Restricting the LibreOffice Java class path settings to local file system schemes (file:// URLs) prevents the execution of untrusted code from remote network locations. Alternatively, disabling the Java Runtime Environment (JRE) in LibreOffice options (Tools -> Options -> LibreOffice -> Advanced) eliminates the attack vector.

notes.text:
An update for libreoffice is now available for Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9.

Red Hat Product Security has rated this update as having a security impact of Important. A Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS) base score, which gives a detailed severity rating, is available for each vulnerability from the CVE link(s) in the References section.
notes.title: Topic

notes.text:
LibreOffice is an open source, community-developed office productivity suite. It includes key desktop applications, such as a word processor, a spreadsheet, a presentation manager, a formula editor, and a drawing program. LibreOffice replaces OpenOffice and provides a similar but enhanced and extended office suite.

Security Fix(es):

* libreoffice: heap buffer overflow in PDF import stream handling (CVE-2026-63274)

* libreoffice: stack buffer overflow in CFF to Type 1 font conversion (CVE-2026-63276)

* libreoffice: stack buffer overflow in CFF font hint handling (CVE-2026-63275)

* libreoffice: libreoffice: Arbitrary code execution via remote Java database driver (CVE-2026-63277)

For more details about the security issue(s), including the impact, a CVSS score, acknowledgments, and other related information, refer to the CVE page(s) listed in the References section.

notes.text: A flaw was found in LibreOffice. When a user imports a specially crafted PDF document with LibreOffice Draw, a heap-based buffer overflow can occur due to improper validation of the stream length. This issue can cause memory corruption, resulting in an application crash.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: libreoffice: heap buffer overflow in PDF import stream handling
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
To exploit this issue, an attacker needs to convince a user to import a specially crafted PDF document. This flaw can cause memory corruption, resulting in an application crash. However, the possibility of arbitrary code execution is not discarded. For these reasons, this vulnerability has been rated with a moderate severity.

Default Red Hat Enterprise Linux security features, including SELinux enforcement, Address Space Layout Randomization (ASLR) and NX (No-Execute) stack protection, significantly increase the difficulty of achieving arbitrary code execution, limiting the impact of this vulnerability.

notes.text: The CVSS score(s) listed for this vulnerability do not reflect the associated product's status, and are included for informational purposes to better understand the severity of this vulnerability.

notes.text: A flaw was found in LibreOffice. When linking spreadsheet cell ranges to external data sources in Calc, a document can specify an external Java database driver. By convincing a user to open a specially crafted document, a remote attacker can force the application to download and execute untrusted Java code from a remote location, resulting in arbitrary code execution.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: libreoffice: libreoffice: Arbitrary code execution via remote Java database driver
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Vulnerability in LibreOffice Calc allows execution of untrusted Java code via remote Java database driver paths in spreadsheet cell range links. When an attacker tricks a user into opening a specially crafted spreadsheet document, Calc downloads and executes arbitrary remote Java code under the security context of the logged-in user.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: The CVSS score(s) listed for this vulnerability do not reflect the associated product's status, and are included for informational purposes to better understand the severity of this vulnerability.
notes.title: CVSS score applicability

remediations.details:
For details on how to apply this update, which includes the changes described in this advisory, refer to:

https://access.redhat.com/articles/11258

Restricting the LibreOffice Java class path settings to local file system schemes (file:// URLs) prevents the execution of untrusted code from remote network locations. Alternatively, disabling the Java Runtime Environment (JRE) in LibreOffice options (Tools -> Options -> LibreOffice -> Advanced) eliminates the attack vector.

descriptions.value:
HTTP::Session versions before 0.54 for Perl allow memcached command injection via unfiltered session ids in HTTP::Session::Store::CHI.

The session id from the client's cookie reaches the CHI cache unchanged. The sibling HTTP::Session::Store::Memcached rejects ids that contain control characters, but the CHI store has no such check, and CHI does not escape keys for its memcached drivers.

With a memcached driver, a CR and LF in the session id end the cache command early, and the server reads the bytes after them as further commands.

descriptions.description: CWE-93 Improper Neutralization of CRLF Sequences

notes.text: A flaw was found in chromium-browser. An out-of-bounds write vulnerability exists within the ANGLE graphics component, allowing a remote attacker to trigger out-of-bounds memory access by providing a specially crafted HTML page. This allows an attacker to potentially manipulate memory contents. The vulnerability is triggered by processing malicious graphics instructions. This can lead to unexpected program behavior.

A remote attacker, after compromising the renderer process, could exploit an uninitialized use vulnerability by crafting a malicious HTML page. This could lead to the leakage of sensitive cross-origin data, potentially exposing information from other websites or applications.

notes.text: A flaw was found in Google Chrome's ANGLE component on Android. A remote attacker could exploit an out-of-bounds memory access vulnerability by enticing a user to visit a specially crafted HTML page. This could potentially allow the attacker to escape the browser's security sandbox, leading to further compromise of the system.

notes.text: A flaw was found in Skia, a 2D graphics library used in Google Chrome. A remote attacker, after compromising the renderer process, could exploit an uninitialized use vulnerability by crafting a malicious HTML page. This could lead to the disclosure of sensitive cross-origin data.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: chromium-browser: skia: chromium-browser: skia: Information disclosure via uninitialized use in Google Chrome
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: A moderate severity information disclosure flaw was found in Skia, the 2D graphics library used by Google Chrome and by WebKitGTK in Red Hat Enterprise Linux. An uninitialized memory use in Skia allows a remote attacker who has already compromised the browser's renderer process to leak cross-origin data when a user visits a crafted HTML page. Red Hat assessed this flaw as having moderate impact rather than upstream's High rating because exploitation requires the attacker to have already compromised the renderer process, so the flaw primarily enables information disclosure across the same-origin policy boundary rather than an initial compromise. In Red Hat Enterprise Linux 7, 8, and 9, the webkit2gtk3 and webkitgtk4 components that bundle Skia are affected, and fixes are being pursued through the upstream WebKitGTK project; Red Hat's Firefox and Thunderbird packages are not affected because the vulnerable code is not present in the Skia copies they ship. The chromium package in Fedora and EPEL (Community Projects) is also affected, with updates handled through the community channels.

notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: chromium-browser: skia: chromium-browser: skia: Cross-origin data leakage via uninitialized use
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: A flaw of important impact was found in Skia, the graphics library used by Chromium and bundled in WebKit-based rendering engines. Uninitialized memory use in Skia allows a remote attacker who has already compromised the renderer process to leak sensitive cross-origin data when the victim views a crafted HTML page, bypassing the same-origin policy and exposing confidential data across origins. In Red Hat Enterprise Linux the flaw is reachable through the webkit2gtk3 component, and a fix is being pursued for the affected streams. Firefox in Red Hat Enterprise Linux is not affected because the vulnerable code is not in the execute path, and Thunderbird and the webkitgtk4 package in Red Hat Enterprise Linux 7 are not affected because the vulnerable code is not present. The community-maintained chromium and webkitgtk packages in Fedora and EPEL are also affected, and fixes are pursued through those channels. Red Hat rated this flaw Important (CVSS 7.4), which is consistent with the upstream Chromium severity of High; CISA assigned a lower CVSS score (3.1, Low), reflecting high attack complexity, low confidentiality impact, and unchanged scope in its vector.

notes.text: A flaw was found in Skia, a 2D graphics library. A remote attacker, who has already compromised the renderer process, could exploit a use-after-free vulnerability by providing a specially crafted HTML page. This could lead to the execution of arbitrary code within the sandbox environment, potentially allowing further system compromise.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: chromium-browser: skia: chromium-browser: skia: Arbitrary code execution via crafted HTML page
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: An IMPORTANT severity use-after-free flaw was found in Skia, a 2D graphics library used for graphics rendering in web browsers and email clients, affecting multiple Red Hat products. A remote attacker who has already compromised the renderer process of an application using Skia could exploit this flaw by tricking a user into loading a specially crafted HTML page, triggering a use-after-free that allows the attacker to execute arbitrary code within the application's sandbox and potentially achieve further system compromise. Because exploitation requires the attacker to already control the renderer process, Red Hat scores this flaw with a local attack vector and scope change (CVSS 8.2, IMPORTANT), while upstream Google rates the corresponding Chromium issue as High severity. Red Hat products that bundle affected Skia code are impacted, including the chromium, firefox, thunderbird, and webkitgtk component families across Red Hat Enterprise Linux, Fedora, and EPEL; Thunderbird in the RHEL 8 BRP is not affected. Fixes for the affected products are being pursued.

Do not process or load untrusted web content with WebKitGTK.

In Red Hat Enterprise Linux 7, the following packages require WebKitGTK4: evolution-data-server, glade, gnome-boxes, gnome-initial-setup, gnome-online-accounts, gnome-shell, shotwell, sushi and yelp.

This vulnerability can only be exploited when these packages are installed in the system and being used via a graphical interface to process untrusted web content, via GNOME for example. In gnome-shell, the vulnerability can be exploited by an attacker from the local network without user interaction.

To mitigate this vulnerability, consider removing these packages. Note that some of these packages are required by GNOME, removing them will also remove GNOME and other packages, breaking functionality. However, the server can still be used via the terminal interface.

Additionally, WebKitGTK3 is not required by any package. Therefore, it can be removed without consequences or break of functionality.

Additionally, WebKitGTK3 is not required by any package. Therefore, it can be removed without consequences or break of functionality.

Within Red Hat deployments, exposure is primarily limited to graphical systems running applications that embed the WebKitGTK rendering engine. Minimal server environments operating without desktop packages or embedded browser components do not process external web content and are therefore not exposed.

Do not process or load untrusted web content with WebKitGTK.

In Red Hat Enterprise Linux 7, the following packages require WebKitGTK4: evolution-data-server, glade, gnome-boxes, gnome-initial-setup, gnome-online-accounts, gnome-shell, shotwell, sushi and yelp.

This vulnerability can only be exploited when these packages are installed in the system and being used via a graphical interface to process untrusted web content, via GNOME for example. In gnome-shell, the vulnerability can be exploited by an attacker from the local network without user interaction.

To mitigate this vulnerability, consider removing these packages. Note that some of these packages are required by GNOME, removing them will also remove GNOME and other packages, breaking functionality. However, the server can still be used via the terminal interface.

Additionally, WebKitGTK3 is not required by any package. Therefore, it can be removed without consequences or break of functionality.

notes.text: A flaw was found in Skia, a 2D graphics library used in Google Chrome. A remote attacker, after compromising the renderer process, could exploit an uninitialized use vulnerability by crafting a malicious HTML page. This could lead to the disclosure of sensitive cross-origin data.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: chromium-browser: skia: chromium-browser: skia: Information disclosure via uninitialized use in Google Chrome
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: A moderate severity information disclosure flaw was found in Skia, the 2D graphics library used by Google Chrome and by WebKitGTK in Red Hat Enterprise Linux. An uninitialized memory use in Skia allows a remote attacker who has already compromised the browser's renderer process to leak cross-origin data when a user visits a crafted HTML page. Red Hat assessed this flaw as having moderate impact rather than upstream's High rating because exploitation requires the attacker to have already compromised the renderer process, so the flaw primarily enables information disclosure across the same-origin policy boundary rather than an initial compromise. In Red Hat Enterprise Linux 7, 8, and 9, the webkit2gtk3 and webkitgtk4 components that bundle Skia are affected, and fixes are being pursued through the upstream WebKitGTK project; Red Hat's Firefox and Thunderbird packages are not affected because the vulnerable code is not present in the Skia copies they ship. The chromium package in Fedora and EPEL (Community Projects) is also affected, with updates handled through the community channels.

notes.text: A flaw was found in Skia in Google Chrome. This uninitialized use vulnerability allows a remote attacker, who has already compromised the renderer process, to craft a malicious HTML page. Successful exploitation can lead to the leakage of sensitive cross-origin data.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: chromium-browser: skia: chromium-browser: skia: Cross-origin data leakage via uninitialized use
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: A flaw of important impact was found in Skia, the graphics library used by Chromium and bundled in WebKit-based rendering engines. Uninitialized memory use in Skia allows a remote attacker who has already compromised the renderer process to leak sensitive cross-origin data when the victim views a crafted HTML page, bypassing the same-origin policy and exposing confidential data across origins. In Red Hat Enterprise Linux the flaw is reachable through the webkit2gtk3 component, and a fix is being pursued for the affected streams. Firefox in Red Hat Enterprise Linux is not affected because the vulnerable code is not in the execute path, and Thunderbird and the webkitgtk4 package in Red Hat Enterprise Linux 7 are not affected because the vulnerable code is not present. The community-maintained chromium and webkitgtk packages in Fedora and EPEL are also affected, and fixes are pursued through those channels. Red Hat rated this flaw Important (CVSS 7.4), which is consistent with the upstream Chromium severity of High; CISA assigned a lower CVSS score (3.1, Low), reflecting high attack complexity, low confidentiality impact, and unchanged scope in its vector.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: A flaw was found in Skia, a 2D graphics library. A remote attacker, who has already compromised the renderer process, could exploit a use-after-free vulnerability by providing a specially crafted HTML page. This could lead to the execution of arbitrary code within the sandbox environment, potentially allowing further system compromise.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: chromium-browser: skia: chromium-browser: skia: Arbitrary code execution via crafted HTML page
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: An IMPORTANT severity use-after-free flaw was found in Skia, a 2D graphics library used for graphics rendering in web browsers and email clients, affecting multiple Red Hat products. A remote attacker who has already compromised the renderer process of an application using Skia could exploit this flaw by tricking a user into loading a specially crafted HTML page, triggering a use-after-free that allows the attacker to execute arbitrary code within the application's sandbox and potentially achieve further system compromise. Because exploitation requires the attacker to already control the renderer process, Red Hat scores this flaw with a local attack vector and scope change (CVSS 8.2, IMPORTANT), while upstream Google rates the corresponding Chromium issue as High severity. Red Hat products that bundle affected Skia code are impacted, including the chromium, firefox, thunderbird, and webkitgtk component families across Red Hat Enterprise Linux, Fedora, and EPEL; Thunderbird in the RHEL 8 BRP is not affected. Fixes for the affected products are being pursued.

Do not process or load untrusted web content with WebKitGTK.

In Red Hat Enterprise Linux 7, the following packages require WebKitGTK4: evolution-data-server, glade, gnome-boxes, gnome-initial-setup, gnome-online-accounts, gnome-shell, shotwell, sushi and yelp.

This vulnerability can only be exploited when these packages are installed in the system and being used via a graphical interface to process untrusted web content, via GNOME for example. In gnome-shell, the vulnerability can be exploited by an attacker from the local network without user interaction.

To mitigate this vulnerability, consider removing these packages. Note that some of these packages are required by GNOME, removing them will also remove GNOME and other packages, breaking functionality. However, the server can still be used via the terminal interface.

Additionally, WebKitGTK3 is not required by any package. Therefore, it can be removed without consequences or break of functionality.

A remote attacker, who has already compromised the renderer process, could exploit a buffer overflow vulnerability by tricking a user into visiting a specially crafted HTML page. On Red Hat Enterprise Linux, this impact is primarily restricted to desktop environments and applications utilizing WebKitGTK, leaving default headless server installations unaffected.

While exploitation requires user interaction to process a maliciously crafted web document, the resulting sandbox escape presents severe risk to client systems.

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as an Important impact for Red Hat Enterprise Linux because successful exploitation requires user interaction to navigate to a malicious web page, yet allows code execution within the rendering sandbox. The flaw stems from memory corruption in the ANGLE graphics translation library, primarily affecting graphical desktop systems where users actively process untrusted web pages. Typical enterprise server deployments lacking graphical user interfaces or web browsing applications are not exposed to this vulnerability under standard configurations.

notes.text: chromium-browser: angle: Chromium: Web origin policy bypass via uninitialized resource in ANGLE
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as having a Critical impact because successful exploitation bypasses the same-origin policy, breaking the core isolation model of web platforms and potentially exposing cross-domain sensitive data. In Red Hat Enterprise Linux environments, exposure is restricted to graphical workstations or applications utilizing embedded WebKitGTK rendering libraries when processing untrusted web content. Headless server installations do not run graphical web rendering engines by default, substantially limiting exposure across enterprise deployments.

notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as having Important impact for Red Hat Enterprise Linux because successful exploitation allows an attacker to bypass browser process isolation and leak sensitive memory across security boundaries, despite requiring user interaction. While Google Chrome is not distributed by Red Hat, the underlying ANGLE graphics translation layer is integrated into embedded web engines such as WebKitGTK used by desktop applications. Standard enterprise server deployments without graphical environments do not expose this surface, and standalone web browsers like Mozilla Firefox do not incorporate the affected subsystem.

notes.text: chromium-browser: angle: ANGLE: Arbitrary code execution via use after free
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as Critical severity for Red Hat products because an unauthenticated remote attacker can escape the application sandbox to execute arbitrary code on the underlying host. On standard Red Hat Enterprise Linux server installations, graphical rendering libraries such as WebKitGTK and Chromium are not installed or invoked by default unless workstation packages or desktop environments are explicitly selected. Triggering the flaw requires a local user to process a malicious, attacker-controlled web page in a vulnerable web rendering application. However, the ability to break isolation boundaries and achieve full host code execution justifies the Critical rating for environments where these desktop components are active.

notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as Critical severity for Red Hat products because an attacker can achieve remote code execution and escape sandbox containment without requiring system privileges. While initially reported in Chromium, the defective ANGLE graphics translation layer is integrated into WebKitGTK packages shipped in Red Hat Enterprise Linux. In typical enterprise environments, WebKitGTK is invoked by graphical applications rendering external web content, exposing users who interact with malicious web resources to complete application or system compromise.

Do not process or load untrusted web content with WebKitGTK.

In Red Hat Enterprise Linux 7, the following packages require WebKitGTK4: evolution-data-server, glade, gnome-boxes, gnome-initial-setup, gnome-online-accounts, gnome-shell, shotwell, sushi and yelp.

This vulnerability can only be exploited when these packages are installed in the system and being used via a graphical interface to process untrusted web content, via GNOME for example. In gnome-shell, the vulnerability can be exploited by an attacker from the local network without user interaction.

To mitigate this vulnerability, consider removing these packages. Note that some of these packages are required by GNOME, removing them will also remove GNOME and other packages, breaking functionality. However, the server can still be used via the terminal interface.

Additionally, WebKitGTK3 is not required by any package. Therefore, it can be removed without consequences or break of functionality.

vulnerabilities.title: chromium-browser: angle: Out of bounds memory access in ANGLE

notes.text: A flaw was found in chromium-browser. An out-of-bounds write vulnerability exists within the ANGLE graphics component, allowing a remote attacker to trigger out-of-bounds memory access by providing a specially crafted HTML page. This allows an attacker to potentially manipulate memory contents. The vulnerability is triggered by processing malicious graphics instructions. This can lead to unexpected program behavior.

vulnerabilities.title: chromium-browser: angle: Chromium: Sandbox escape via out-of-bounds write in ANGLE

notes.text: A flaw was found in Google Chrome's ANGLE component on Android. A remote attacker could exploit an out-of-bounds memory access vulnerability by enticing a user to visit a specially crafted HTML page. This could potentially allow the attacker to escape the browser's security sandbox, leading to further compromise of the system.

Exploitation requires user interaction, where a victim must visit a specially crafted HTML page, enabling an attacker to execute arbitrary code outside the browser's security sandbox. This bypasses security boundaries, leading to potential compromise of the underlying system.

Do not process or load untrusted web content with WebKitGTK.

In Red Hat Enterprise Linux 7, the following packages require WebKitGTK4: evolution-data-server, glade, gnome-boxes, gnome-initial-setup, gnome-online-accounts, gnome-shell, shotwell, sushi and yelp.

This vulnerability can only be exploited when these packages are installed in the system and being used via a graphical interface to process untrusted web content, via GNOME for example. In gnome-shell, the vulnerability can be exploited by an attacker from the local network without user interaction.

To mitigate this vulnerability, consider removing these packages. Note that some of these packages are required by GNOME, removing them will also remove GNOME and other packages, breaking functionality. However, the server can still be used via the terminal interface.

Additionally, WebKitGTK3 is not required by any package. Therefore, it can be removed without consequences or break of functionality.

Do not process or load untrusted web content with WebKitGTK.

In Red Hat Enterprise Linux 7, the following packages require WebKitGTK4: evolution-data-server, glade, gnome-boxes, gnome-initial-setup, gnome-online-accounts, gnome-shell, shotwell, sushi and yelp.

This vulnerability can only be exploited when these packages are installed in the system and being used via a graphical interface to process untrusted web content, via GNOME for example. In gnome-shell, the vulnerability can be exploited by an attacker from the local network without user interaction.

To mitigate this vulnerability, consider removing these packages. Note that some of these packages are required by GNOME, removing them will also remove GNOME and other packages, breaking functionality. However, the server can still be used via the terminal interface.

Additionally, WebKitGTK3 is not required by any package. Therefore, it can be removed without consequences or break of functionality.

notes.text: A flaw was found in ANGLE, a component of Google Chrome. Improper input validation could allow a remote attacker to execute arbitrary code outside of the browser's security sandbox by enticing a user to visit a specially crafted HTML page. This could lead to a complete compromise of the affected system.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: chromium-browser: angle: ANGLE in Google Chrome: Arbitrary code execution via improper input validation
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as having Critical impact for Red Hat products because a remote, unauthenticated attacker could escape the client sandbox and execute arbitrary instructions on the host environment. In Red Hat Enterprise Linux, the affected ANGLE graphics translation layer is integrated into the WebKitGTK (webkit2gtk3) library, which powers local desktop and rendering utilities. Successful exploitation depends on an interactive user loading malicious web content, meaning server installations operating without graphical components are not exposed.

Typical enterprise server deployments lacking graphical user interfaces or web browsing applications are not exposed to this vulnerability under standard configurations.

Headless server installations do not run graphical web rendering engines by default, substantially limiting exposure across enterprise deployments.

notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as Critical severity for Red Hat products because an unauthenticated remote attacker can escape the application sandbox to execute arbitrary code on the underlying host. On standard Red Hat Enterprise Linux server installations, graphical rendering libraries such as WebKitGTK and Chromium are not installed or invoked by default unless workstation packages or desktop environments are explicitly selected. Triggering the flaw requires a local user to process a malicious, attacker-controlled web page in a vulnerable web rendering application. However, the ability to break isolation boundaries and achieve full host code execution justifies the Critical rating for environments where these desktop components are active.

Do not process or load untrusted web content with WebKitGTK.

In Red Hat Enterprise Linux 7, the following packages require WebKitGTK4: evolution-data-server, glade, gnome-boxes, gnome-initial-setup, gnome-online-accounts, gnome-shell, shotwell, sushi and yelp.

This vulnerability can only be exploited when these packages are installed in the system and being used via a graphical interface to process untrusted web content, via GNOME for example. In gnome-shell, the vulnerability can be exploited by an attacker from the local network without user interaction.

To mitigate this vulnerability, consider removing these packages. Note that some of these packages are required by GNOME, removing them will also remove GNOME and other packages, breaking functionality. However, the server can still be used via the terminal interface.

Additionally, WebKitGTK3 is not required by any package. Therefore, it can be removed without consequences or break of functionality.

vulnerabilities.title: chromium-browser: skia: chromium-browser: skia: Use after free in Skia

notes.text: A flaw was found in chromium-browser. An out-of-bounds write vulnerability exists within the ANGLE graphics component, allowing a remote attacker to trigger out-of-bounds memory access by providing a specially crafted HTML page. This allows an attacker to potentially manipulate memory contents. The vulnerability is triggered by processing malicious graphics instructions. This can lead to unexpected program behavior.

notes.text: A flaw was found in Skia, a 2D graphics library used in Google Chrome. A remote attacker, after compromising the renderer process, could exploit an uninitialized use vulnerability by crafting a malicious HTML page. This could lead to the disclosure of sensitive cross-origin data.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: chromium-browser: skia: chromium-browser: skia: Information disclosure via uninitialized use in Google Chrome
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: A moderate severity information disclosure flaw was found in Skia, the 2D graphics library used by Google Chrome and by WebKitGTK in Red Hat Enterprise Linux. An uninitialized memory use in Skia allows a remote attacker who has already compromised the browser's renderer process to leak cross-origin data when a user visits a crafted HTML page. Red Hat assessed this flaw as having moderate impact rather than upstream's High rating because exploitation requires the attacker to have already compromised the renderer process, so the flaw primarily enables information disclosure across the same-origin policy boundary rather than an initial compromise. In Red Hat Enterprise Linux 7, 8, and 9, the webkit2gtk3 and webkitgtk4 components that bundle Skia are affected, and fixes are being pursued through the upstream WebKitGTK project; Red Hat's Firefox and Thunderbird packages are not affected because the vulnerable code is not present in the Skia copies they ship. The chromium package in Fedora and EPEL (Community Projects) is also affected, with updates handled through the community channels.

notes.text: chromium-browser: skia: chromium-browser: skia: Cross-origin data leakage via uninitialized use
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: A flaw of important impact was found in Skia, the graphics library used by Chromium and bundled in WebKit-based rendering engines. Uninitialized memory use in Skia allows a remote attacker who has already compromised the renderer process to leak sensitive cross-origin data when the victim views a crafted HTML page, bypassing the same-origin policy and exposing confidential data across origins. In Red Hat Enterprise Linux the flaw is reachable through the webkit2gtk3 component, and a fix is being pursued for the affected streams. Firefox in Red Hat Enterprise Linux is not affected because the vulnerable code is not in the execute path, and Thunderbird and the webkitgtk4 package in Red Hat Enterprise Linux 7 are not affected because the vulnerable code is not present. The community-maintained chromium and webkitgtk packages in Fedora and EPEL are also affected, and fixes are pursued through those channels. Red Hat rated this flaw Important (CVSS 7.4), which is consistent with the upstream Chromium severity of High; CISA assigned a lower CVSS score (3.1, Low), reflecting high attack complexity, low confidentiality impact, and unchanged scope in its vector.

A remote attacker, who has already compromised the renderer process, could exploit a use-after-free vulnerability by providing a specially crafted HTML page. This could lead to the execution of arbitrary code within the sandbox environment, potentially allowing further system compromise.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: chromium-browser: skia: chromium-browser: skia: Arbitrary code execution via crafted HTML page
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: An IMPORTANT severity use-after-free flaw was found in Skia, a 2D graphics library used for graphics rendering in web browsers and email clients, affecting multiple Red Hat products. A remote attacker who has already compromised the renderer process of an application using Skia could exploit this flaw by tricking a user into loading a specially crafted HTML page, triggering a use-after-free that allows the attacker to execute arbitrary code within the application's sandbox and potentially achieve further system compromise. Because exploitation requires the attacker to already control the renderer process, Red Hat scores this flaw with a local attack vector and scope change (CVSS 8.2, IMPORTANT), while upstream Google rates the corresponding Chromium issue as High severity. Red Hat products that bundle affected Skia code are impacted, including the chromium, firefox, thunderbird, and webkitgtk component families across Red Hat Enterprise Linux, Fedora, and EPEL; Thunderbird in the RHEL 8 BRP is not affected. Fixes for the affected products are being pursued.

Do not process or load untrusted web content with WebKitGTK.

In Red Hat Enterprise Linux 7, the following packages require WebKitGTK4: evolution-data-server, glade, gnome-boxes, gnome-initial-setup, gnome-online-accounts, gnome-shell, shotwell, sushi and yelp.

This vulnerability can only be exploited when these packages are installed in the system and being used via a graphical interface to process untrusted web content, via GNOME for example. In gnome-shell, the vulnerability can be exploited by an attacker from the local network without user interaction.

To mitigate this vulnerability, consider removing these packages. Note that some of these packages are required by GNOME, removing them will also remove GNOME and other packages, breaking functionality. However, the server can still be used via the terminal interface.

Additionally, WebKitGTK3 is not required by any package. Therefore, it can be removed without consequences or break of functionality.

Do not process or load untrusted web content with WebKitGTK.

In Red Hat Enterprise Linux 7, the following packages require WebKitGTK4: evolution-data-server, glade, gnome-boxes, gnome-initial-setup, gnome-online-accounts, gnome-shell, shotwell, sushi and yelp.

This vulnerability can only be exploited when these packages are installed in the system and being used via a graphical interface to process untrusted web content, via GNOME for example. In gnome-shell, the vulnerability can be exploited by an attacker from the local network without user interaction.

To mitigate this vulnerability, consider removing these packages. Note that some of these packages are required by GNOME, removing them will also remove GNOME and other packages, breaking functionality. However, the server can still be used via the terminal interface.

Additionally, WebKitGTK3 is not required by any package. Therefore, it can be removed without consequences or break of functionality.

notes.text: A flaw was found in Skia, a 2D graphics library used in Google Chrome. A remote attacker, after compromising the renderer process, could exploit an uninitialized use vulnerability by crafting a malicious HTML page. This could lead to the disclosure of sensitive cross-origin data.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: chromium-browser: skia: chromium-browser: skia: Information disclosure via uninitialized use in Google Chrome
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: A moderate severity information disclosure flaw was found in Skia, the 2D graphics library used by Google Chrome and by WebKitGTK in Red Hat Enterprise Linux. An uninitialized memory use in Skia allows a remote attacker who has already compromised the browser's renderer process to leak cross-origin data when a user visits a crafted HTML page. Red Hat assessed this flaw as having moderate impact rather than upstream's High rating because exploitation requires the attacker to have already compromised the renderer process, so the flaw primarily enables information disclosure across the same-origin policy boundary rather than an initial compromise. In Red Hat Enterprise Linux 7, 8, and 9, the webkit2gtk3 and webkitgtk4 components that bundle Skia are affected, and fixes are being pursued through the upstream WebKitGTK project; Red Hat's Firefox and Thunderbird packages are not affected because the vulnerable code is not present in the Skia copies they ship. The chromium package in Fedora and EPEL (Community Projects) is also affected, with updates handled through the community channels.

notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: chromium-browser: skia: chromium-browser: skia: Cross-origin data leakage via uninitialized use
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: A flaw of important impact was found in Skia, the graphics library used by Chromium and bundled in WebKit-based rendering engines. Uninitialized memory use in Skia allows a remote attacker who has already compromised the renderer process to leak sensitive cross-origin data when the victim views a crafted HTML page, bypassing the same-origin policy and exposing confidential data across origins. In Red Hat Enterprise Linux the flaw is reachable through the webkit2gtk3 component, and a fix is being pursued for the affected streams. Firefox in Red Hat Enterprise Linux is not affected because the vulnerable code is not in the execute path, and Thunderbird and the webkitgtk4 package in Red Hat Enterprise Linux 7 are not affected because the vulnerable code is not present. The community-maintained chromium and webkitgtk packages in Fedora and EPEL are also affected, and fixes are pursued through those channels. Red Hat rated this flaw Important (CVSS 7.4), which is consistent with the upstream Chromium severity of High; CISA assigned a lower CVSS score (3.1, Low), reflecting high attack complexity, low confidentiality impact, and unchanged scope in its vector.

notes.text: A flaw was found in Skia, a 2D graphics library. A remote attacker, who has already compromised the renderer process, could exploit a use-after-free vulnerability by providing a specially crafted HTML page. This could lead to the execution of arbitrary code within the sandbox environment, potentially allowing further system compromise.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: chromium-browser: skia: chromium-browser: skia: Arbitrary code execution via crafted HTML page
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: An IMPORTANT severity use-after-free flaw was found in Skia, a 2D graphics library used for graphics rendering in web browsers and email clients, affecting multiple Red Hat products. A remote attacker who has already compromised the renderer process of an application using Skia could exploit this flaw by tricking a user into loading a specially crafted HTML page, triggering a use-after-free that allows the attacker to execute arbitrary code within the application's sandbox and potentially achieve further system compromise. Because exploitation requires the attacker to already control the renderer process, Red Hat scores this flaw with a local attack vector and scope change (CVSS 8.2, IMPORTANT), while upstream Google rates the corresponding Chromium issue as High severity. Red Hat products that bundle affected Skia code are impacted, including the chromium, firefox, thunderbird, and webkitgtk component families across Red Hat Enterprise Linux, Fedora, and EPEL; Thunderbird in the RHEL 8 BRP is not affected. Fixes for the affected products are being pursued.

Do not process or load untrusted web content with WebKitGTK.

In Red Hat Enterprise Linux 7, the following packages require WebKitGTK4: evolution-data-server, glade, gnome-boxes, gnome-initial-setup, gnome-online-accounts, gnome-shell, shotwell, sushi and yelp.

This vulnerability can only be exploited when these packages are installed in the system and being used via a graphical interface to process untrusted web content, via GNOME for example. In gnome-shell, the vulnerability can be exploited by an attacker from the local network without user interaction.

To mitigate this vulnerability, consider removing these packages. Note that some of these packages are required by GNOME, removing them will also remove GNOME and other packages, breaking functionality. However, the server can still be used via the terminal interface.

Additionally, WebKitGTK3 is not required by any package. Therefore, it can be removed without consequences or break of functionality.

In Red Hat Enterprise Linux 7, the following packages require WebKitGTK4: evolution-data-server, glade, gnome-boxes, gnome-initial-setup, gnome-online-accounts, gnome-shell, shotwell, sushi and yelp.

This vulnerability can only be exploited when these packages are installed in the system and being used via a graphical interface to process untrusted web content, via GNOME for example. In gnome-shell, the vulnerability can be exploited by an attacker from the local network without user interaction.

To mitigate this vulnerability, consider removing these packages. Note that some of these packages are required by GNOME, removing them will also remove GNOME and other packages, breaking functionality. However, the server can still be used via the terminal interface.

Additionally, WebKitGTK3 is not required by any package. Therefore, it can be removed without consequences or break of functionality.

Do not process or load untrusted web content with WebKitGTK.

In Red Hat Enterprise Linux 7, the following packages require WebKitGTK4: evolution-data-server, glade, gnome-boxes, gnome-initial-setup, gnome-online-accounts, gnome-shell, shotwell, sushi and yelp.

This vulnerability can only be exploited when these packages are installed in the system and being used via a graphical interface to process untrusted web content, via GNOME for example. In gnome-shell, the vulnerability can be exploited by an attacker from the local network without user interaction.

To mitigate this vulnerability, consider removing these packages. Note that some of these packages are required by GNOME, removing them will also remove GNOME and other packages, breaking functionality. However, the server can still be used via the terminal interface.

Additionally, WebKitGTK3 is not required by any package. Therefore, it can be removed without consequences or break of functionality.

Do not process or load untrusted web content with WebKitGTK.

In Red Hat Enterprise Linux 7, the following packages require WebKitGTK4: evolution-data-server, glade, gnome-boxes, gnome-initial-setup, gnome-online-accounts, gnome-shell, shotwell, sushi and yelp.

This vulnerability can only be exploited when these packages are installed in the system and being used via a graphical interface to process untrusted web content, via GNOME for example. In gnome-shell, the vulnerability can be exploited by an attacker from the local network without user interaction.

To mitigate this vulnerability, consider removing these packages. Note that some of these packages are required by GNOME, removing them will also remove GNOME and other packages, breaking functionality. However, the server can still be used via the terminal interface.

Additionally, WebKitGTK3 is not required by any package. Therefore, it can be removed without consequences or break of functionality.

https://access.redhat.com/articles/11258

Do not process or load untrusted web content with WebKitGTK.

In Red Hat Enterprise Linux 7, the following packages require WebKitGTK4: evolution-data-server, glade, gnome-boxes, gnome-initial-setup, gnome-online-accounts, gnome-shell, shotwell, sushi and yelp.

This vulnerability can only be exploited when these packages are installed in the system and being used via a graphical interface to process untrusted web content, via GNOME for example. In gnome-shell, the vulnerability can be exploited by an attacker from the local network without user interaction.

To mitigate this vulnerability, consider removing these packages. Note that some of these packages are required by GNOME, removing them will also remove GNOME and other packages, breaking functionality. However, the server can still be used via the terminal interface.

Additionally, WebKitGTK3 is not required by any package. Therefore, it can be removed without consequences or break of functionality.

notes.text: chromium-browser: skia: chromium-browser: skia: Information disclosure via uninitialized use in Google Chrome
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: A moderate severity information disclosure flaw was found in Skia, the 2D graphics library used by Google Chrome and by WebKitGTK in Red Hat Enterprise Linux. An uninitialized memory use in Skia allows a remote attacker who has already compromised the browser's renderer process to leak cross-origin data when a user visits a crafted HTML page. Red Hat assessed this flaw as having moderate impact rather than upstream's High rating because exploitation requires the attacker to have already compromised the renderer process, so the flaw primarily enables information disclosure across the same-origin policy boundary rather than an initial compromise. In Red Hat Enterprise Linux 7, 8, and 9, the webkit2gtk3 and webkitgtk4 components that bundle Skia are affected, and fixes are being pursued through the upstream WebKitGTK project; Red Hat's Firefox and Thunderbird packages are not affected because the vulnerable code is not present in the Skia copies they ship. The chromium package in Fedora and EPEL (Community Projects) is also affected, with updates handled through the community channels.

notes.text: chromium-browser: skia: chromium-browser: skia: Cross-origin data leakage via uninitialized use
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: A flaw of important impact was found in Skia, the graphics library used by Chromium and bundled in WebKit-based rendering engines. Uninitialized memory use in Skia allows a remote attacker who has already compromised the renderer process to leak sensitive cross-origin data when the victim views a crafted HTML page, bypassing the same-origin policy and exposing confidential data across origins. In Red Hat Enterprise Linux the flaw is reachable through the webkit2gtk3 component, and a fix is being pursued for the affected streams. Firefox in Red Hat Enterprise Linux is not affected because the vulnerable code is not in the execute path, and Thunderbird and the webkitgtk4 package in Red Hat Enterprise Linux 7 are not affected because the vulnerable code is not present. The community-maintained chromium and webkitgtk packages in Fedora and EPEL are also affected, and fixes are pursued through those channels. Red Hat rated this flaw Important (CVSS 7.4), which is consistent with the upstream Chromium severity of High; CISA assigned a lower CVSS score (3.1, Low), reflecting high attack complexity, low confidentiality impact, and unchanged scope in its vector.

notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: An IMPORTANT severity use-after-free flaw was found in Skia, a 2D graphics library used for graphics rendering in web browsers and email clients, affecting multiple Red Hat products. A remote attacker who has already compromised the renderer process of an application using Skia could exploit this flaw by tricking a user into loading a specially crafted HTML page, triggering a use-after-free that allows the attacker to execute arbitrary code within the application's sandbox and potentially achieve further system compromise. Because exploitation requires the attacker to already control the renderer process, Red Hat scores this flaw with a local attack vector and scope change (CVSS 8.2, IMPORTANT), while upstream Google rates the corresponding Chromium issue as High severity. Red Hat products that bundle affected Skia code are impacted, including the chromium, firefox, thunderbird, and webkitgtk component families across Red Hat Enterprise Linux, Fedora, and EPEL; Thunderbird in the RHEL 8 BRP is not affected. Fixes for the affected products are being pursued.

In Red Hat Enterprise Linux 7, the following packages require WebKitGTK4: evolution-data-server, glade, gnome-boxes, gnome-initial-setup, gnome-online-accounts, gnome-shell, shotwell, sushi and yelp.

This vulnerability can only be exploited when these packages are installed in the system and being used via a graphical interface to process untrusted web content, via GNOME for example. In gnome-shell, the vulnerability can be exploited by an attacker from the local network without user interaction.

To mitigate this vulnerability, consider removing these packages. Note that some of these packages are required by GNOME, removing them will also remove GNOME and other packages, breaking functionality. However, the server can still be used via the terminal interface.

Additionally, WebKitGTK3 is not required by any package. Therefore, it can be removed without consequences or break of functionality.

Do not process or load untrusted web content with WebKitGTK.

In Red Hat Enterprise Linux 7, the following packages require WebKitGTK4: evolution-data-server, glade, gnome-boxes, gnome-initial-setup, gnome-online-accounts, gnome-shell, shotwell, sushi and yelp.

This vulnerability can only be exploited when these packages are installed in the system and being used via a graphical interface to process untrusted web content, via GNOME for example. In gnome-shell, the vulnerability can be exploited by an attacker from the local network without user interaction.

To mitigate this vulnerability, consider removing these packages. Note that some of these packages are required by GNOME, removing them will also remove GNOME and other packages, breaking functionality. However, the server can still be used via the terminal interface.

Additionally, WebKitGTK3 is not required by any package. Therefore, it can be removed without consequences or break of functionality.

Do not process or load untrusted web content with WebKitGTK.

In Red Hat Enterprise Linux 7, the following packages require WebKitGTK4: evolution-data-server, glade, gnome-boxes, gnome-initial-setup, gnome-online-accounts, gnome-shell, shotwell, sushi and yelp.

This vulnerability can only be exploited when these packages are installed in the system and being used via a graphical interface to process untrusted web content, via GNOME for example. In gnome-shell, the vulnerability can be exploited by an attacker from the local network without user interaction.

To mitigate this vulnerability, consider removing these packages. Note that some of these packages are required by GNOME, removing them will also remove GNOME and other packages, breaking functionality. However, the server can still be used via the terminal interface.

Additionally, WebKitGTK3 is not required by any package. Therefore, it can be removed without consequences or break of functionality.

notes.text: A flaw was found in chromium-browser. An out-of-bounds write vulnerability exists within the ANGLE graphics component, allowing a remote attacker to trigger out-of-bounds memory access by providing a specially crafted HTML page. This allows an attacker to potentially manipulate memory contents. The vulnerability is triggered by processing malicious graphics instructions. This can lead to unexpected program behavior.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: chromium-browser: angle: ANGLE Out-of-Bounds Write Vulnerability
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: The CVSS score(s) listed for this vulnerability do not reflect the associated product's status, and are included for informational purposes to better understand the severity of this vulnerability.
notes.title: CVSS score applicability

remediations.details:
For details on how to apply this update, which includes the changes described in this advisory, refer to:

https://access.redhat.com/articles/11258

Mitigation for this issue is either not available or the currently available options do not meet the Red Hat Product Security criteria comprising ease of use and deployment, applicability to widespread installation base or stability.

notes.text: A flaw was found in Google Chrome's ANGLE component on Android. A remote attacker could exploit an out-of-bounds memory access vulnerability by enticing a user to visit a specially crafted HTML page. This could potentially allow the attacker to escape the browser's security sandbox, leading to further compromise of the system.

notes.text: A flaw was found in Skia in Google Chrome. This uninitialized use vulnerability allows a remote attacker, who has already compromised the renderer process, to craft a malicious HTML page. Successful exploitation can lead to the leakage of sensitive cross-origin data.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: chromium-browser: skia: chromium-browser: skia: Cross-origin data leakage via uninitialized use
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: A flaw of important impact was found in Skia, the graphics library used by Chromium and bundled in WebKit-based rendering engines. Uninitialized memory use in Skia allows a remote attacker who has already compromised the renderer process to leak sensitive cross-origin data when the victim views a crafted HTML page, bypassing the same-origin policy and exposing confidential data across origins. In Red Hat Enterprise Linux the flaw is reachable through the webkit2gtk3 component, and a fix is being pursued for the affected streams. Firefox in Red Hat Enterprise Linux is not affected because the vulnerable code is not in the execute path, and Thunderbird and the webkitgtk4 package in Red Hat Enterprise Linux 7 are not affected because the vulnerable code is not present. The community-maintained chromium and webkitgtk packages in Fedora and EPEL are also affected, and fixes are pursued through those channels. Red Hat rated this flaw Important (CVSS 7.4), which is consistent with the upstream Chromium severity of High; CISA assigned a lower CVSS score (3.1, Low), reflecting high attack complexity, low confidentiality impact, and unchanged scope in its vector.

notes.text: A flaw was found in Skia, a 2D graphics library. A remote attacker, who has already compromised the renderer process, could exploit a use-after-free vulnerability by providing a specially crafted HTML page. This could lead to the execution of arbitrary code within the sandbox environment, potentially allowing further system compromise.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: chromium-browser: skia: chromium-browser: skia: Arbitrary code execution via crafted HTML page
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: An IMPORTANT severity use-after-free flaw was found in Skia, a 2D graphics library used for graphics rendering in web browsers and email clients, affecting multiple Red Hat products. A remote attacker who has already compromised the renderer process of an application using Skia could exploit this flaw by tricking a user into loading a specially crafted HTML page, triggering a use-after-free that allows the attacker to execute arbitrary code within the application's sandbox and potentially achieve further system compromise. Because exploitation requires the attacker to already control the renderer process, Red Hat scores this flaw with a local attack vector and scope change (CVSS 8.2, IMPORTANT), while upstream Google rates the corresponding Chromium issue as High severity. Red Hat products that bundle affected Skia code are impacted, including the chromium, firefox, thunderbird, and webkitgtk component families across Red Hat Enterprise Linux, Fedora, and EPEL; Thunderbird in the RHEL 8 BRP is not affected. Fixes for the affected products are being pursued.

Do not process or load untrusted web content with WebKitGTK.

In Red Hat Enterprise Linux 7, the following packages require WebKitGTK4: evolution-data-server, glade, gnome-boxes, gnome-initial-setup, gnome-online-accounts, gnome-shell, shotwell, sushi and yelp.

This vulnerability can only be exploited when these packages are installed in the system and being used via a graphical interface to process untrusted web content, via GNOME for example. In gnome-shell, the vulnerability can be exploited by an attacker from the local network without user interaction.

To mitigate this vulnerability, consider removing these packages. Note that some of these packages are required by GNOME, removing them will also remove GNOME and other packages, breaking functionality. However, the server can still be used via the terminal interface.

Additionally, WebKitGTK3 is not required by any package. Therefore, it can be removed without consequences or break of functionality.

https://access.redhat.com/articles/11258

Do not process or load untrusted web content with WebKitGTK.

In Red Hat Enterprise Linux 7, the following packages require WebKitGTK4: evolution-data-server, glade, gnome-boxes, gnome-initial-setup, gnome-online-accounts, gnome-shell, shotwell, sushi and yelp.

This vulnerability can only be exploited when these packages are installed in the system and being used via a graphical interface to process untrusted web content, via GNOME for example. In gnome-shell, the vulnerability can be exploited by an attacker from the local network without user interaction.

To mitigate this vulnerability, consider removing these packages. Note that some of these packages are required by GNOME, removing them will also remove GNOME and other packages, breaking functionality. However, the server can still be used via the terminal interface.

Additionally, WebKitGTK3 is not required by any package. Therefore, it can be removed without consequences or break of functionality.

Do not process or load untrusted web content with WebKitGTK.

In Red Hat Enterprise Linux 7, the following packages require WebKitGTK4: evolution-data-server, glade, gnome-boxes, gnome-initial-setup, gnome-online-accounts, gnome-shell, shotwell, sushi and yelp.

This vulnerability can only be exploited when these packages are installed in the system and being used via a graphical interface to process untrusted web content, via GNOME for example. In gnome-shell, the vulnerability can be exploited by an attacker from the local network without user interaction.

To mitigate this vulnerability, consider removing these packages. Note that some of these packages are required by GNOME, removing them will also remove GNOME and other packages, breaking functionality. However, the server can still be used via the terminal interface.

Additionally, WebKitGTK3 is not required by any package. Therefore, it can be removed without consequences or break of functionality.

Do not process or load untrusted web content with WebKitGTK.

In Red Hat Enterprise Linux 7, the following packages require WebKitGTK4: evolution-data-server, glade, gnome-boxes, gnome-initial-setup, gnome-online-accounts, gnome-shell, shotwell, sushi and yelp.

This vulnerability can only be exploited when these packages are installed in the system and being used via a graphical interface to process untrusted web content, via GNOME for example. In gnome-shell, the vulnerability can be exploited by an attacker from the local network without user interaction.

To mitigate this vulnerability, consider removing these packages. Note that some of these packages are required by GNOME, removing them will also remove GNOME and other packages, breaking functionality. However, the server can still be used via the terminal interface.

Additionally, WebKitGTK3 is not required by any package. Therefore, it can be removed without consequences or break of functionality.

notes.text: A flaw was found in WebKitGTK. Processing malicious web content can cause an unexpected process crash due to improper memory handling.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: webkitgtk: Processing maliciously crafted web content may lead to an unexpected process crash
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
To exploit this issue, an attacker needs to trick a user into processing or loading malicious web content. Due to this reason, this flaw has been rated with an important severity.
Additionally, this issue can cause an unexpected process crash but the possibility of remote code execution is not discarded.
notes.title: Statement

notes.title: CVSS score applicability

https://access.redhat.com/articles/11258

Do not process or load untrusted web content with WebKitGTK.

In Red Hat Enterprise Linux 7, the following packages require WebKitGTK4: evolution-data-server, glade, gnome-boxes, gnome-initial-setup, gnome-online-accounts, gnome-shell, shotwell, sushi and yelp.

This vulnerability can only be exploited when these packages are installed in the system and being used via a graphical interface to process untrusted web content, via GNOME for example. In gnome-shell, the vulnerability can be exploited by an attacker from the local network without user interaction.

To mitigate this vulnerability, consider removing these packages. Note that some of these packages are required by GNOME, removing them will also remove GNOME and other packages, breaking functionality. However, the server can still be used via the terminal interface.

Additionally, WebKitGTK3 is not required by any package. Therefore, it can be removed without consequences or break of functionality.

https://access.redhat.com/articles/11258

Do not process or load untrusted web content with WebKitGTK.

In Red Hat Enterprise Linux 7, the following packages require WebKitGTK4: evolution-data-server, glade, gnome-boxes, gnome-initial-setup, gnome-online-accounts, gnome-shell, shotwell, sushi and yelp.

This vulnerability can only be exploited when these packages are installed in the system and being used via a graphical interface to process untrusted web content, via GNOME for example. In gnome-shell, the vulnerability can be exploited by an attacker from the local network without user interaction.

To mitigate this vulnerability, consider removing these packages. Note that some of these packages are required by GNOME, removing them will also remove GNOME and other packages, breaking functionality. However, the server can still be used via the terminal interface.

Additionally, WebKitGTK3 is not required by any package. Therefore, it can be removed without consequences or break of functionality.

notes.text:
WebKitGTK+ is port of the WebKit portable web rendering engine to the GTK+ platform. These packages provide WebKitGTK+ for GTK+ 3.

notes.text: A flaw was found in WebKitGTK. Processing malicious web content can cause an unexpected process crash due to improper memory handling.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: webkitgtk: Processing maliciously crafted web content may lead to an unexpected process crash
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
To exploit this issue, an attacker needs to trick a user into processing or loading malicious web content. Due to this reason, this flaw has been rated with an important severity.
Additionally, this issue can cause an unexpected process crash but the possibility of remote code execution is not discarded.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: The CVSS score(s) listed for this vulnerability do not reflect the associated product's status, and are included for informational purposes to better understand the severity of this vulnerability.
notes.title: CVSS score applicability

For details on how to apply this update, which includes the changes described in this advisory, refer to:

https://access.redhat.com/articles/11258

Do not process or load untrusted web content with WebKitGTK.

In Red Hat Enterprise Linux 7, the following packages require WebKitGTK4: evolution-data-server, glade, gnome-boxes, gnome-initial-setup, gnome-online-accounts, gnome-shell, shotwell, sushi and yelp.

This vulnerability can only be exploited when these packages are installed in the system and being used via a graphical interface to process untrusted web content, via GNOME for example. In gnome-shell, the vulnerability can be exploited by an attacker from the local network without user interaction.

To mitigate this vulnerability, consider removing these packages. Note that some of these packages are required by GNOME, removing them will also remove GNOME and other packages, breaking functionality. However, the server can still be used via the terminal interface.

Additionally, WebKitGTK3 is not required by any package. Therefore, it can be removed without consequences or break of functionality.

Do not process or load untrusted web content with WebKitGTK.

In Red Hat Enterprise Linux 7, the following packages require WebKitGTK4: evolution-data-server, glade, gnome-boxes, gnome-initial-setup, gnome-online-accounts, gnome-shell, shotwell, sushi and yelp.

This vulnerability can only be exploited when these packages are installed in the system and being used via a graphical interface to process untrusted web content, via GNOME for example. In gnome-shell, the vulnerability can be exploited by an attacker from the local network without user interaction.

To mitigate this vulnerability, consider removing these packages. Note that some of these packages are required by GNOME, removing them will also remove GNOME and other packages, breaking functionality. However, the server can still be used via the terminal interface.

Additionally, WebKitGTK3 is not required by any package. Therefore, it can be removed without consequences or break of functionality.

Do not process or load untrusted web content with WebKitGTK.

In Red Hat Enterprise Linux 7, the following packages require WebKitGTK4: evolution-data-server, glade, gnome-boxes, gnome-initial-setup, gnome-online-accounts, gnome-shell, shotwell, sushi and yelp.

This vulnerability can only be exploited when these packages are installed in the system and being used via a graphical interface to process untrusted web content, via GNOME for example. In gnome-shell, the vulnerability can be exploited by an attacker from the local network without user interaction.

To mitigate this vulnerability, consider removing these packages. Note that some of these packages are required by GNOME, removing them will also remove GNOME and other packages, breaking functionality. However, the server can still be used via the terminal interface.

Additionally, WebKitGTK3 is not required by any package. Therefore, it can be removed without consequences or break of functionality.

notes.text: A flaw was found in zod. A remote attacker can trigger a denial of service (DoS) by submitting an excessively large array of invalid items to an application that validates input schemas without length constraints. Because the validation process accumulates error records for each failing element without a cap or early exit, the application consumes excessive memory and crashes due to an out-of-memory condition.

notes.text: zod: zod: Denial of service via unbounded array validation
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is evaluated with an Important severity because remote attackers can induce complete service unavailability through process termination without requiring privileged access. Within Red Hat environments, the affected library is embedded into multiple management consoles and microservices that process structured user data. The operational impact depends on whether exposed network endpoints evaluate untrusted collections without preliminary restrictions on payload sizes or element counts.

notes.text: A flaw was found in SQLite's FTS5 full-text search extension. This vulnerability involves memory corruption, specifically an out-of-bounds read and a heap buffer overflow, which can be triggered by supplying a crafted database with malformed FTS5 page data. When an FTS5 MATCH query is executed against such a database, an attacker can cause process crashes, memory exhaustion, or achieve arbitrary code execution, potentially compromising the system.

Exploitation requires an application to process a specially crafted SQLite database containing malformed FTS5 page data, which could occur if an attacker provides a malicious database to a vulnerable application. This risk is elevated in scenarios where applications handle untrusted SQLite database files.

notes.text: A flaw was found in fast-uri. This vulnerability arises because fast-uri does not correctly interpret backslash characters as authority delimiters in Uniform Resource Locators (URLs), unlike Node.js's native WHATWG URL parser. This discrepancy can cause applications that use fast-uri for security policy enforcement, such as allowlists or Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) filtering, to misidentify the intended host. Consequently, an attacker could bypass these security policies, potentially redirecting traffic to unintended internal or sensitive network destinations.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: fast-uri: Fast-uri: Security policy bypass due to URL parsing inconsistency
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Important: This flaw in fast-uri allows for a security policy bypass due to inconsistent URL parsing between fast-uri and Node.js's native WHATWG URL parser. Applications within Red Hat Hardened Images that rely on fast-uri for host-based policy enforcement, such as allowlists or Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) filtering, can be misled by specially crafted URLs. This could enable an attacker to redirect traffic to unintended internal or sensitive network destinations.

An attacker who controls the contents of an archive can exploit this by including symbolic links, allowing them to create or overwrite files at arbitrary locations on the system where the archive is being extracted. This could lead to unauthorized modification of system files or potentially arbitrary code execution.

notes.text: A validation flaw has been discovered in the python cryptography package. This missing validation allows an attacker to provide a public key point P from a small-order subgroup. This can lead to security issues in various situations, such as the most commonly used signature verification (ECDSA) and shared key negotiation (ECDH). When the victim computes the shared secret as S = [victim_private_key]P via ECDH, this leaks information about victim_private_key mod (small_subgroup_order). For curves with cofactor > 1, this reveals the least significant bits of the private key. When these weak public keys are used in ECDSA , it's easy to forge signatures on the small subgroup. Only SECT curves are impacted by this.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This flaw, while difficult to exploit, would lead to a loss of integrity in the encrypted communication channel. Given that the cryptography package is a library, it is likely to be used in situations that do not require user interaction.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the HTTP/2 protocol implementation within the Go standard library (golang.org/x/net and net/http/internal/http2). A remote attacker can exploit this vulnerability by sending a specially crafted HTTP/2 SETTINGS frame with the SETTINGS_MAX_FRAME_SIZE parameter set to zero. notes.text: A flaw was found in fflate. A remote attacker could exploit this vulnerability by providing a specially crafted ZIP archive. This archive, when processed, can lead to an infinite loop during decompression, causing a Denial of Service (DoS) condition. This occurs because a malformed central directory entry in the ZIP archive causes out-of-bounds reads, which keeps a processing loop permanently active.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: fflate: fflate: Denial of Service via crafted ZIP archives
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
This CVE describes a denial-of-service flaw in the fflate JavaScript compression library. Parsing a maliciously crafted ZIP archive via unzipSync()/unzip() triggers an infinite loop in the ZIP64 central-directory parser (z64e): a central directory entry declaring the ZIP64 size sentinel (0xFFFFFFFF) but omitting the required ZIP64 extra field causes out-of-bounds reads that keep the loop condition permanently true, consuming CPU indefinitely. Only fflate's ZIP-extraction APIs are affected; its gzip/deflate/zip-creation paths are not.

Red Hat products bundle fflate almost exclusively within web-frontend assets. Each affected component was assessed individually. Components that reach fflate only through compression-only consumers (posthog-js gzip telemetry, jsPDF zlib) never invoke the vulnerable unzipSync/z64e path and are marked not affected (vulnerable code not in the execute path). Components that bundle fflate in the vulnerable version range (through 0.8.2) where the ZIP-extraction path could not be positively excluded are marked affected. Where the vulnerable path is reachable only from client-side browser code processing same-origin assets, practical impact is limited to a self-inflicted denial of service within the user's own browser session rather than a service-level outage.
notes.title: Statement
